transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Start time: 15:30 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (AetherWorks CTO), Maya (Lead ML Eng), Carlos (Infra), Sofia (Prod Ops)

Auto Summary: Quick scouting call for model selection and infra options. Focus on 8k vs 32k context, multilingual NLU for EN/ES/PT, and tool-calling to external billing systems.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, joining with Priya on the SE side. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Liam: Good, thanks. Excited to chat. We are trying to figure out which model path and hosting mode makes sense for AetherWorks.
[00:18] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda — gather context about your workloads, tokens per request, multilingual needs, tool-calling, any compliance constraints, and then Priya will run through tradeoffs.
[00:27] Maya: Sounds good. I'll jump in with numbers later, but our key driver is large multi-doc summarization and question answering across English and Spanish customer tickets, sometimes Portuguese. Typical session has 6–15 documents, average 2.5k tokens, but we do get bursts up to 22k when threading long history.
[00:42] Priya: Ok that already suggests you might need beyond 8k in some flows. Quick clarifying, when you say 22k, is that raw tokens after concatenation or after some prefiltering?
[00:51] Maya: That's raw, we haven't done smart chunking in production; it's an area we want to improve but we don't want to re-architect the whole pipeline immediately.
[01:02] Carlos: And on infra side, we are very sensitive to data residency and audit logs. We have a SOC2 in progress, and for some customers we need log retention for 90 days.
[01:11] Jordan: Good, good. That pushes Private or Dedicated as likely candidates, but let's talk cost/latency tradeoffs first. Priya, want to walk model options?
[01:20] Priya: Sure. So for open models we typically talk about several families — Llama-based, Mistral and some of the larger Mixtral-like models on Hugging Face. Llama 2/3 style forks get you good instruction following, Mistral gives great zero-shot perf on some NLU tasks. For 8k contexts it's straightforward, for 32k you need compiled runtime and KV cache behavior tuned.
[01:37] Maya: Quick question — we saw mention of Redwood-verified quantized variants. How close are they to FP16 in quality? Last time we tested some 4-bit variants there was a small hallucination regression.
[01:47] Priya: Yeah, important callout. Our quantization profiles are workload-aware — for classification and QA they typically match FP16 on accuracy metrics within noise, but generation heavy tasks and chain-of-thought can show regressions. We recommend a shadow run before switching. We'll include evaluation metrics in the report.
[02:00] Sofia: And tool-calling — we want the model to call internal billing APIs and also run a step that queries a vector DB for recent tickets. Is that supported for Hosted?
[02:10] Priya: Tool-calling is supported on Hosted. For Hosted we sandbox outbound calls and provide a secure connector model. For enterprise-grade connectors or on-prem database access, Private deployment is the safest; Dedicated can do private connectors via peered VPCs, depends on the network setup.
[02:24] Carlos: For peered VPCs, do you require us to open wide egress or can we do strict IP restrictions? Our firewall rules are quite strict.
[02:32] Priya: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink-like flows. You'll provide a network diagram and we can work with your infra team to limit CIDR ranges. We also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest in Private.
[02:44] Liam: How does Redwood route requests when capacity is constrained? We don't want silent fallback to a weaker model without approval.
[02:53] Jordan: Good question — rollouts and fallback policy is configurable. By default Redwood will not silently downgrade your model; there are policies for canary vs auto-fallback and you can pin versions. We'll show the console controls.
[03:04] Priya: Back to model selection — given the token distributions Maya mentioned, a hybrid approach makes sense: use an 8k-sized optimized model for most interactive workflows and 32k variants for batch summarization. Also caching prefixes and pre-computing embeddings for retrieval can reduce token consumption.
[03:22] Maya: For multilingual accuracy, do you recommend a single multilingual model or an ensemble of language-specific smaller models?
[03:30] Priya: If your volume per language is moderate, a single well-optimized multilingual model often works. But fine-tuning or instruction-tuning per language improves F1/precision in edge cases. Another option is language detection and routing to language-specific endpoints in Redwood; we've seen that help for specialized vocab.
[03:46] Carlos: When you say caching prefixes, are you talking about the KV cache being persisted between requests? We are worried about memory blow up with 32k concurrency.
[03:55] Priya: Not persist beyond session, but prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts or shared context is available. Also, Redwood's runtime does continuous batching and will evict or compress KV entries for long sequences; this helps but you should still model expected concurrency. For very high concurrency with long contexts Dedicated with reserved GPU pools is the sweet spot.
[04:16] Liam: Can you give rough ballpark latency numbers for a 4k token generation on Hosted vs Dedicated? Just order-of-magnitude.
[04:24] Priya: Ballpark — Hosted with shared capacity for 4k generation at p95 maybe 600–900ms per token for some large models is not right phrasing. Sorry, per token is off. For 4k generation end-to-end request latency depends on generation length. For a typical 300-token response on an 8k context, p95 could be 600–900ms on Dedicated and 900–1400ms on Hosted depending on load and model. We'll run benchmarks to give you exact numbers.
[04:50] Maya: That's big delta. Cost-wise, what are we looking at for production scale (couple hundred thousand requests/month)?
[04:58] Jordan: We'll include pricing examples in the sheet — Hosted has per-token pricing and variable unit economics, Dedicated is reserved capacity with much lower marginal cost for heavy steady throughput, and Private is licensing plus infra cost. We'll put a cost model in the doc.
[05:12] Sofia: On security — logs, redaction, can Redwood redact PII before storing?
[05:18] Priya: Yes, we support request/response redaction and token-level redaction hooks. For Private you control retention; for Hosted we offer configurable retention windows and redaction policies. We also emit audit logs and support SAML SSO and role-based access controls.
[05:32] Liam: Any gotchas for on-prem connectors with tool-calls? We need to call internal SOAP systems sometimes.
[05:39] Priya: For legacy systems we recommend a small gateway service inside your network that Redwood's tool-calling connector will invoke via the peered path. The gateway translates to REST and handles auth. It's a common pattern.
[05:50] Maya: Ok practical next steps — we want you to run a benchmark using our representative prompts across 8k and 32k modes, and include multilingual samples. Also include a test of tool-calling flow against a sandboxed endpoint.
[06:03] Jordan: Great — Priya will own benchmark setup. Maya, can you share 100 sample prompts and token histograms?
[06:10] Maya: Yes, I'll curate and anonymize them.
[06:13] Carlos: I'll pull network diagrams and constraints for the VPC.
[06:16] Priya: One more thing — for the 32k path be explicit about how much of the sequence is context vs generation. Sometimes customers keep too much context by default. A small prefiltering step reduces cost dramatically.
[06:28] Maya: Yeah, agreed. We'll do some heuristics.
[06:31] [08:12] Jordan: (briefly summarizes) So agreed: Redwood will run a 24–72 hour benchmark across two model families and context lengths, deliver performance and cost estimates, and send security and pricing docs. AetherWorks will share prompts and infra details.
[08:25] Liam: Sounds good. Quick safety — do you support per-request data deletion? Some of our clients require prompt-level erasure.
[08:33] Priya: Yes, request-level delete is possible in Private; for Hosted we have retention windows and deletion APIs — we'll include details.
[08:40] Maya: Also curious about evals — can Redwood attach our eval sets so we get regression alerts on new model rollouts?
[08:47] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize integrates evals and can alert on quality regressions tied to saved prompt sets. We can show the dashboard in the next session.
[09:00] [24:00] (conversation continues — deeper into KV cache and batching internals; SE explains kernel selection and compilation optimizations, some technical terms are slightly garbled in the transcript)
[24:15] Priya: Our runtime selects kernels and optimizes attention for long sequences; we do a dynamic tradeoff between memory and compute and sometimes choose fused kernels for lower latency.
[24:30] Maya: Could you provide a simplified explanation we can hand to infra?
[24:36] Priya: Sure — I'll make a one-page that explains how batching, KV cache, and eviction work, and what to expect for GPU memory when using 32k context.
[24:43] Jordan: Cool, action items and owners we'll capture and send. Any final questions?
[24:50] Liam: Timeline-wise, if benchmarks look good we'd aim to start a POC in July and decide on Dedicated vs Private by late Q3.
[24:59] Jordan: Noted. We'll be in touch with dates for the benchmark kickoff and a deeper technical session. Thanks everyone.
[25:08] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: Some acronyms and model names are slightly off — e.g., MultIral vs Mixtral transcription. Also occasional speaker mis-attribution for fast back-and-forth.
